statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail 11% (low), Stress 50% (elevated), Confidence 86% (high), dominant mode mixed. NQZ26 retested the 30,957.50 session low at 30,965.00 in the 12:30Z bar, held, and recovered to 31,027.75 by 13:27:33Z, 34.00 points below the 31,061.75 prior close, ahead of the 14:00Z ISM Services release.
recommendation: Tail at 11% sits well below the 25% block threshold, so the deterministic mapping yields EA_ON and green for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. The narrow evidence-based danger window spans 13:45Z to 15:00Z, covering the S&P Global PMI finals, the 14:00Z September ISM Services release and the first hour of repricing that follows. Published Tail peaks at 15% in the 14:00Z hour and remains inside the low band across all 24 forecast slots. Stress at 50% is elevated and reflects a 5.30% 10-year yield, a VIX up 4.90% on the day and a euro at a 17-month low on French fiscal stress; none of that has produced the no-retracement price path that defines Tail. Existing-position management and emergency protection remain unaffected by this publication.
headline: Tail 11% as NQZ26 holds its 30,957.50 session low on a 30,965.00 retest and recovers to 31,027.75, 0.11% under the prior close, into the 14:00Z ISM Services print
body:
The prior hour published Tail at 7% on a 29.75-point coil with four rising intraday lows. That sequence has since been broken, but in the benign direction. Between 12:25Z and 12:40Z NQZ26 sold off to 30,965.00, undercutting the 31,007.25 and 30,986.00 lows that had defined the rising sequence, and stopped 7.50 points above the 09:40Z session low of 30,957.50. The retest held. Price then recovered about 63 points, closing the 13:10Z bar at 31,019.25 and printing 31,027.75 at 13:27:33Z.

A failed probe of a session low followed by a recovery is the opposite of the repeated-extension shape that defines Tail. The day's range is 263.75 points, 30,957.50 to 31,221.25, and the last print sits near its middle, 34.00 points or 0.11% below the 31,061.75 prior close and 193.50 points below the overnight high. There is no persistent directional efficiency in either direction, and no evidence of failed retracements. Tail rises from 7% to 11% only because the current clock-hour contains the 13:30Z US cash open, which the available delayed futures feed does not yet cover, and because the 13:45Z S&P Global PMI finals and the 14:00Z ISM Services release follow inside the danger window.

Cross-asset alignment is partial rather than confirming. The 10-year Treasury yield is 5.30%, up about two basis points, with the 2-year at 4.84%; an elevated long end is a persistent valuation headwind for Nasdaq megacaps but has not been accompanied by an equity break. VIX is 16.06, up 4.90% from a 15.31 close, which is a higher reading at a still-low absolute level. WTI is 89.54, down 1.73%, and Brent is 101.78, so energy is not adding an inflation impulse today, while gold at 4,179.90 is up 0.42%. The clearest stress sits in Europe rather than the US: the euro touched 1.1161, a 17-month low, with the French-German 10-year spread near 146 basis points and contagion visible in Belgian and Italian debt. In Nasdaq single names, Cerebras rose sharply in the pre-market after OpenAI's chief executive described the company as a close partner, an example of idiosyncratic AI-hardware flow that has not translated into index-level direction.

Stress is raised from 46% to 50% for the event stack and the European sovereign backdrop. It describes a difficult environment that can still mean-revert and does not by itself change the mapped policy state. Confidence is 86%: current index, volatility, yield, energy and calendar levels were all verified against primary sources this hour, and the seven-day US calendar through 12 October was re-verified. Two limits apply. The futures quote feed used here runs roughly ten minutes behind and ends at 13:27:33Z, so the 13:30Z cash open is not yet observed and is treated as a checkpoint rather than as evidence. The shared Finviz context file carries a collection timestamp of 29 September and a partial collection status, so it is far outside the 90-minute freshness window and was excluded from this assessment; the evidence above comes entirely from independent current research.

lookbackSummary: The 24 hours to 12:00Z contain 23 published Claude assessments and one gap at 06:00Z, which stays explicitly unavailable with null assessment fields. The first nine hours, 13:00Z to 21:00Z on 4 October, held Tail flat at 3% while Stress ran from 66% up to 71%, the signature of a difficult but orderly regime. Tail then stepped up through the Globex reopen to 12% at 22:00Z and peaked at 15% in the 01:00Z hour as the 31,221.25 overnight high was set and left behind. From 02:00Z the path decayed steadily, 13%, 10%, 8%, 8%, reaching 6% at 08:00Z with Stress falling from 60% to 48%. The European morning produced the only genuine amplification of the window: 11% and mixed at 09:00Z, then 14% and trend-down at 10:00Z on a sequence of lower highs, before the 30,957.50 low held, the sequence broke, and the path returned to 9% at 11:00Z and 7% at 12:00Z. Every available slot in the window mapped to EA_ON and green.
outlookSummary: The 24-hour published path runs from 11% now to a peak of 15% in the 14:00Z hour, down to a 7% overnight floor, and finishes at 10% in the 12:00Z hour tomorrow, so every slot maps to EA_ON and green. The elevation is concentrated in the 14:00Z and 15:00Z hours and is a conditional allowance for the S&P Global PMI finals and the September ISM Services release, not an assertion that one-way structure has been observed. Stress peaks at 56% alongside it and decays to a 40% overnight trough before rebuilding to 49% into the next US pre-market. Confidence declines from 86% to a 60% floor with the horizon, marking the point beyond which no price-path evidence exists. Only the current 13:00Z slot states observed structure as fact: the 30,965.00 retest of the 30,957.50 session low and the recovery to 31,027.75 by 13:27:33Z. The 13:30Z US cash open falls inside that hour but is not yet visible in the delayed futures feed, so it is framed as a checkpoint rather than as an observation.
